messages.subject: BNC file names
messages.body_plain:
How can r access each file in the BNC? The way they named the files is very complex.

Probably what I want to do is create a one-time program that writes the name of each file to, say, bnc-filenames.txt, and then whenever I want it I can load that file into a vector and scroll through it with a single FOR loop, but is there a *relatively* easy way to create this initial list?

I'm dealing with linux and the BNC XML edition. Have the World edition as well.

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D, ACB, ALB
Korea Maritime University
Schoolmasters: http://grou.ps/schoolmasters/
National Korea Toastmasters: http://grou.ps/koreatoastmasters

messages.body_plain:
> but is there a *relatively* easy way to create this initial list?

Use dir(topmostdirectoryofBNC, full.names=TRUE, recursive=TRUE)

STG

Can I find them somewhere else, perhaps online?

messages.body_plain:
The Kindle edition has enither page numbers nor pages. Alan, go to location 1004 for the directions.

The Kindle edition has a few quirks. Reference to an R command within a paragraph is not distinguished. So you get sentences like 'use paste to combine each word.' I imagine the print edition has a different font for 'paste' or something.

Also the codes are not searchable.

On the other hand, it sure is great not to have to prop the book open when typing those codes!

messages.subject: Change of website
messages.body_plain:
Given Google's already pathetic support of the Pages and Files
features of Google groups over the last year or so, it's not really a
big surprise that they are now going to discontinue that 'service' as
of 1 November 2010. For now, the Discussion feature should remain
available, and as before you can find a mirror of this group's page
with all the files at <http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries/
research/qclwr/qclwr.html>

Sorry for that, I had trusted Google more than was appropriate, it
seems ...

STG
